questions.q: What does Kabir lament when he sees the grinding stones at work?
questions.answer: He weeps because, just as grain is crushed between two millstones, every living being is crushed between life's opposing forces such as joy and sorrow, birth and death. Nothing remains whole.

questions.q: What lesson does Kabir teach in 'Bura Jo Dekhan Main Chala'?
questions.answer: He looked for wicked people but found none; when he looked into his own heart he found himself the worst. We should examine our own faults before judging others.

questions.q: What does Kabir want to teach through the example of the date tree?
questions.answer: A date palm is tall but gives no shade and its fruit is out of reach. Greatness or wealth is worthless unless it benefits others; true worth lies in usefulness.

questions.q: How, according to Kabir, does one become truly wise?
questions.answer: Not by reading many books and scriptures, but by understanding and practising love — the 'two and a half letters' of prem. One who knows love is the true scholar.

questions.q: What does Thiruvalluvar say about harsh speech?
questions.answer: Speaking harsh words when sweet words would serve is like eating unripe fruit when ripe fruit is at hand. A wound made by the tongue never heals, unlike a burn.

questions.q: What six things make a ruler 'a lion among kings', according to Thiruvalluvar?
questions.answer: An army, a loyal people, wealth, a wise minister, friends and a fort. A ruler who has all six is strong and respected like a lion among kings.

questions.q: What common values do Kabir and Thiruvalluvar teach?
questions.answer: Both teach humility, kind and truthful speech, self-reflection, contentment rather than greed, and compassion for all, and both promoted harmony among communities.

questions.q: Compare the themes of Kabir and Thiruvalluvar.
questions.answer: Both stress humility and self-examination, gentle and truthful speech, contentment and right conduct. Kabir focuses on love of God, impermanence and equanimity, using everyday images. Thiruvalluvar gives practical guidance on household life, governance, learning and self-discipline.

questions.q: Explain Kabir's doha on remembering God in joy and sorrow.
questions.answer: People remember God only when they suffer and forget Him when they are happy. Kabir says that if one remembers God in joy too, one stays balanced and never feels crushed by sorrow.

or.q: Explain Thiruvalluvar's kural on the lotus and the mind.
or.answer: The lotus stem grows as the flood water rises, so the flower always stays above water. In the same way a person's greatness rises with the height of his mind — his thoughts and character, not his wealth, measure his worth.

questions.q: What does Thiruvalluvar say leads a person to ruin? How can a student avoid it?
questions.answer: Delay, forgetfulness, sloth and excessive sleep are a 'pleasure-boat' that carries people to ruin. A student can avoid them by planning work and doing it on time, keeping notes and reminders, staying active and sleeping only as much as needed.
